documents.title: Doc 60 - Infringement - Car 16 - Causing a collision with Car 44
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 16 - Causing a collision with Car 44

details.fact: Car 16 collided with Car 44 at Turn 7.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video and in-car video evidence. Car 16 attempted to overtake Car 44 on the inside at Turn 7. The Stewards noted that Car 16 initiated the overtaking manoeuvre from a considerable distance behind Car 44, attempting to position his car on the inside. In assessing the incident, the Stewards also took into account the FIA Driving Standards Guidelines, in particular the criteria applicable to overtaking manoeuvres on the inside of a corner. The Stewards determined that the front axle of Car 16 was not at least alongside the mirror of Car 44 at the apex of the corner. The Stewards therefore determined that Car 16 had not earned the right to the corner at Turn 7 and was wholly to blame for the resulting collision. Accordingly, the Stewards imposed a 10-second time penalty.

documents.title: Doc 54 - Infringement - Car 44 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 44 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 44 left the track at Turn 8 at 20:22, while defending a position and gained a lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video, timing and in-car video evidence. Car 1 (NOR) attempted to overtake Car 44 (HAM) on the left-hand side approaching Turn 7. At the apex, the front axle of Car 1 was at least alongside of the mirror of Car 44. Applying the Driving Standards Guidelines, the Stewards determined that Car 1 was entitled to the corner. Car 44 remained alongside Car 1 and subsequently crossed the white line on the right-hand side, leaving the track. By doing so, Car 44 avoided a potential collision but maintained its position ahead of Car 1. By leaving the track while defending, Car 44 therefore is considered as having gained a lasting advantage. Car 44 did not concede the position to Car 1, as he should have done. The Stewards therefore determined that Car 44 had left the track and gained a lasting advantage.

documents.title: Doc 45 - Infringement - Car 41 Unsafe Release
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 41 Unsafe Release

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: Car 41 was released in an unsafe manner into the path of Car 23.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.6.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: The competitor (Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team) is fined €5,000.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. Car 41 (LIN) was released from its pit position into the path of Car 23 (ALB), which was approaching in the fast lane. The Stewards determined that this constituted an unsafe release. During the hearing, the team representative acknowledged that the release was unsafe and explained that a malfunction of the radio communication system had affected the coordination of the release procedure. The Stewards accepted this explanation and acknowledged that the communication failure was not intentional. However, the circumstances leading to the release do not alter the fact that Car 41 was released into the path of another car. The Stewards noted that reliable communication is an important element of a safe release procedure and that appropriate backup arrangements should be available in the event of a communication failure.

documents.title: Doc 44 - Decision - Qualifying SC2-SC1 Times
documents.subject: Decision - Qualifying SC2-SC1 Times

details.fact: The F1 Cars below exceeded the 2:00.0 time limit between the Safety Car lines.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code (non-compliance with the Race Director’s Competition Notes, item 1, document 12).
details.reason: The Stewards thoroughly reviewed Marshalling/Positioning data, timing data, on-board cameras and CCTV cameras. All drivers concerned stayed at or above speeds necessary to stay below 2:00.0 around the vast majority of the circuit. However, in all cases the Stewards determined that the drivers took appropriate actions to not impede other drivers, and in all cases, they slowed down significantly to allow other drivers to pass while giving those drivers a clear track. The Stewards therefore determine that all drivers concerned did not drive “unnecessarily slowly”, and that they were above the maximum time because they took appropriate steps, and we therefore take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 38 - Decision - Alleged Driving Erratically
documents.subject: Decision - Alleged Driving Erratically

details.fact: Car 3 engaged in a series of moves on the entry of T17 in front of Car 43
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), team representative and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. Both cars were on out laps approaching the corner, with Car 3 (VER) ahead of Car 43 (COL). Car 3 was weaving from side to side while Car 43 approached from behind at a slightly higher speed. As Car 43 completed the overtaking, Car 3 moved toward the the right-hand side of the track and Car 43 passed on the left. The driver of Car 3 explained that he was weaving to warm his tyres up and that he could not use more energy due to issues he had with his engine earlier in the lap. In contrast, the driver of Car 43 deployed a significant amount of energy which allowed him to overtake Car 3 and caught the driver of Car 3 by surprise. He stated that he had not expected Car 43 to attempt an overtake because both were on a preparation lap and approaching the last turn. Once he became aware of the overtaking manoeuvre, he remained on the right-hand side of the track to allow Car 43 to pass without issue. The Stewards considered the movements (i. e. weaving) of Car 3, the fact that Car 3 experienced some issues with the engine earlier in the lap and that it had an impact on the energy deployment, the fact that both cars were on out laps, the relative speeds of the two cars and the circumstances of the overtaking manoeuvre which was ultimately completed without issue. The Stewards acknowledged that weaving to maintain tyre temperature is common during the preparation for a flying lap. In this case, when the driver of Car 3 realised that Car 43 was overtaking, he immediately stopped the weaving and maintained his position on the right-hand side and allowed Car 43 to pass. Taking into account the issue that lead to a lack of energy deployment, the relatively small speed differential and the absence of any further movement towards Car 43, the Stewards concluded that there were mitigating elements. The Stewards therefore determined to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 37 - Infringement - Car 3 - Erratic Driving in Turn 14
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 3 - Erratic Driving in Turn 14

details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), the driver of Car 63 (George Russell), team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. Both cars were approaching Turn 14, with Car 3 ahead of Car 63. Car 3 braked earlier than expected and changed direction under braking. Car 63, approaching from behind, moved to the left and attempted to overtake on the inside. During the manoeuvre, the front axle of Car 63 was ahead of the mirror of Car 3. The two cars subsequently made contact. During the hearing, the drivers also discussed the informal gentlemen's agreements concerning the preparation for a flying lap and the conduct expected between drivers in such situations. The Stewards noted these explanations but considered that such informal understandings were of limited relevance to the assessment of the incident. The decisive considerations were the actual movements of both cars and their relative positions. The Stewards therefore examined the braking and change of direction of Car 3, the evasive manoeuvre and positioning of Car 63 and taking into account the applicable Driving Standards Guidelines. The Stewards considered that Car 3's change of direction under braking was unpredictable and contributed to the situation in which Car 63 had to move to the inside to avoid contact. While the Stewards did not consider the manoeuvre sufficiently serious to warrant a more severe penalty, they concluded that changing direction under braking in these circumstances fell below the standard of driving expected. Taking into account the circumstances of the incident, the Stewards determined that a Driver Warning was appropriate.

documents.title: Doc 36 - Infringement - Car 23 - Erratic Driving in Turn 17
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 23 - Erratic Driving in Turn 17

details.fact: Car 23 was driven erratically in an incident involving Car 6 at Turn 17
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 23 (Alexander Albon), team representative and reviewed video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. Both cars were approaching Turn 17, with Car 23 (ALB) ahead of Car 6 (HAD). Car 23 was weaving to try keeping temperature in the tyres and preparing for his next flying lap. Car 6 approached from behind at a significantly higher speed, with a speed differential of approximately 60 km/h. As the cars approached Turn 17, Car 23 moved towards the inside of the corner to take his normal racing line, but into the path of Car 6. The driver of Car 6 had to brake heavily to avoid a collision. The driver of Car 23 explained that he was preparing for his next flying lap and needed to maintain tyre temperature while also managing his battery status. He stated that he had not expected Car 6 to close so quickly. The Stewards considered the movements of Car 23, the significant speed differential between the two cars and the need for Car 6 to take evasive action. In particular, the Stewards examined whether the driving of Car 23 was unpredictable or potentially dangerous, taking into account the circumstances of his preparation for the following lap. The Stewards acknowledged that weaving to maintain tyre temperature is common when preparing for a flying lap. However, drivers must remain aware of approaching traffic and ensure that their movements do not create potentially dangerous situations. In this case, Car 23 moved towards the inside of Turn 17 while Car 6 was approaching at a significantly higher speed, forcing the driver of Car 6 to brake heavily to avoid contact. The Stewards considered this movement to be unpredictable and potentially dangerous, irrespective of the driver's intention to prepare for his next flying lap. The Stewards therefore determined that the driving of Car 23 constituted erratic driving and imposed a driving reprimand.

details.decision: Drop of 35 grid positions for the next Race in which the driver participates.
details.reason: The penalty is imposed in accordance with Article B8.2.8 of the FIA F1 Regulations. In this case, the use of the (MGU-K) carries a 5 grid place penalty by virtue of Article B8.2.8 b) of the FIA F1 Regulations and the use of the (ICE), (TC) and (EXH) additional element(s) carries a 10 grid place penalty by virtue of Article B8.2.8 a) of the FIA F1 Regulations. Therefore, there is an accumulation of 35 places. Subject to Car 87 being classified in the results of Qualifying, Car 87 will be allocated a grid position in the Race in accordance with Article B2.5.4b.iv of the FIA F1 Regulations.
